visual_text: Codes sort admissions. They give no verdict on one resident.
Emergency admissions from a care home
A list of diagnosis codes sorts them
On the list: counted as potentially avoidable
Could the illness have been prevented?
Could it have been treated in the home?
Different lists give different totals: the most commonly used NHS subset has 19 of the 36 conditions found in the research literature (all emergency admissions, England, 2005/6).
Purdy et al, Public Health 2009; Chambers et al, HSDR 2023
alt_text: Flow diagram: emergency admissions from a care home are sorted by a list of diagnosis codes into on the list or not. A panel gives three questions for one resident: preventable, treatable at home, what the person wanted. The most used NHS list has 19 of 36 conditions.
design_instructions: Single card. Left flow: admissions box, arrow, funnel box with orange Service measure tab, arrow, hatched On the list box and plain Not on the list box. Right deep teal panel Individual decision with three numbered questions. Mint strip 19 of 36. Claim C16-18-a.
